instructions: Put a dry skillet over medium heat. Add the 2 tbsp coriander seeds and 1 of the dried chilies and toast them for 2 minutes, shaking the pan now and then.

Add the 1 tsp fennel seeds, the 2 cloves, the 3 cardamom pods, the cinnamon and the 1/4 tsp peppercorns. Toast for 1 more minute, until they smell warm and the coriander is a shade darker. Tip everything onto a plate to cool.
Meanwhile, cut the chicken into 1 inch pieces and pat them dry with paper towels. Toss them in a bowl with 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Finely chop 1 of the onions. Cut the other onion into 1 inch squares and pull the layers apart. Seed the bell pepper and cut it into 1 inch squares.
Grate the 3 tomatoes on the large holes of a box grater and throw away the skins. Grate 1 1/2 tsp of the ginger and mince the 3 garlic cloves.
Slice the green chili thinly and put it in a small bowl for the table.
Grind the cooled spices to a fine powder in a spice grinder. This is your kadai masala.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet or kadai over high heat. Add the onion squares and the bell pepper and stir fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until the pepper has a few blistered spots but is still crunchy. Tip them onto a plate.
Turn the heat to medium and add the remaining 3 tbsp oil to the same pan. Add the 1/2 tsp cumin seeds and break the last dried chili in. After about 20 seconds the seeds will sizzle and smell toasty.
Add the chopped onion and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft and golden.
Stir in the ginger and garlic and cook for under a minute, until they stop smelling raw.
Turn the heat up to medium high and add the chicken. Stir fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until the outsides have turned pale all over.
Turn the heat down to medium low. Add the 1/4 tsp turmeric, the 1/2 tsp chili powder and all of the kadai masala and stir for 30 seconds, so the spices cook in the oil.
Add the grated tomatoes and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens and stops smelling of raw tomato.

Partly cover the pan and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the chicken is cooked through. If it starts to stick, add a splash of water. You're cooking it to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest piece. No thermometer? Cut a thick piece open: it's done when there's no pink left and the juices run clear.
Put the 1/4 cup cream in a small bowl and stir in 3 tbsp of the hot sauce from the pan. Pour it back into the pan and stir it through.

Add the peppers and onion squares back to the pan. Crush the 1 tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan and add the 1/2 tsp garam masala. Simmer for 2 minutes. Any longer and the peppers go soft.
Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro and scatter it over the top. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with naan or basmati rice, with the sliced green chili on the side.
method_notes: Both versions grind a fresh kadai masala from toasted coriander seeds, dried Kashmiri chili, fennel, cloves, cinnamon and pepper, and both stir fry the bell peppers and onion petals separately so they stay crunchy before folding them in at the end. Swasthi's cooks the chicken straight into an onion, ginger garlic and pureed tomato base, finishing with kasuri methi, garam masala and a little cream or yogurt. Sinfully Spicy marinates thighs in yogurt for 2 hours, fries the masala in mustard oil with cumin, bay and cinnamon, and cooks it down dry before adding the vegetables. This one follows Swasthi's, with thighs, grated tomato in place of a blender puree, and the chili on the side.
